canonical_name: SpiralCore transport with ternary FBS binders (float projection form)
aliases: SpiralCore BFS plus Atomic Ternary FBS
plain_what: Instead of mixing every input into every output with learned weights, each output block picks one input block from a small tree of stored blocks, three branches per node, and moves it along a path of exact signed-axis steps in 8-dimensional E8 space. No learned coefficient is multiplied in; the path itself does the transforming.
how_it_works: Input channels are 8D integer atoms kept by a static Rust compiler in ordered ternary (base-3) binders: children, parent links, atom identity, support length and the incomplete frontier (at most 6,560 atoms, 16 frontier roots, 8 stages). SpiralCore supplies the geometry: octonion left actions give 15 Clifford bivector generators B, each a signed coordinate permutation with B^2 = -I, acting on the 16 roots of one E8 anchor orbit through 64 signed operator states. BFS over these labelled edges gives ordered action histories, composed by left-composition; the exact inverse is the reversed sequence with each B cubed. The model stores F32 query points [output_blocks, stages, 8]. At each stage a query picks a root of the fixed orbit by distance, and the BFS history between roots composes the signed action that transports the selected atom's 8 coordinates. Each output block selects ONE input atom and transports it; no coefficient exists for any input/output pair, and exact atom identity stays separate from geometric state. Forward is gather and sign; the input adjoint is the exact inverse action scattered to the selected atom. Query credit is a declared root-edge secant surrogate: force each lawful sibling, reroute its descendants, pair output credit with the carrier displacement, resolve along the edge. It is not the derivative of hard selection. CUDA only; CPU fallback refused.
geometry: E8 root system (one 16-root anchor orbit of the 240 roots); Clifford Cl(0,6) bivectors from octonion left actions (15 edges, 64 signed states); signed-axis permutations; SpiralCore BFS routes and exact inverses; ordered ternary (base-3) FBS binder tree and frontier.

status_reason: The float projection is built and device-qualified at the finite-kernel level (four CUDA, three static-plan and two artifact tests on an RTX 5090, zero absolute error on exact fixtures) and ran inside 18 rung-0 controls; it has never been trained. Secant fitness and language utility are unmeasured. Its integer descendant is ACTIVE in discrete-learning.
reopen_conditions: To activate the float form: a new D37 sheet in a separately scanned float module, with fresh TEST FITNESS: FIT, the owner release that applies, an export gap, and the shared writer and geometric head as dependencies.
Show the secant surrogate gives descent (a falling loss or a comparison with a random-refit control) and that routing is stable; neither has been measured.
Justify the total number of 8D blocks prospectively; record that each output block reads one input atom, so a capacity comparison against a mixing projection is needed.
Fresh transfer and D22 noise requirements for any KEEP; tokens/s on the same CUDA harness against the retired dense arm.

rule_compat.D11: The float F32/BF16 form is not servable. Signed-axis permutations, sign flips and table reads need no multiplier, and the integer descendant in crates/uor-r4-discrete is integer-only on the GPU.
rule_compat.D23: No probability weights, normalised exponentials or learned input/output coefficient grids; selection is hard by distance. no_softmax ratchet 1649/1649 on the delivering PR.
rule_compat.D30: Retires the dense Hamilton contraction; no matmul in the new path (no_matmul ratchet 93/93, down from 95). Static table construction reads no model tensors and is not model compute.
rule_compat.D32_D37: The F32 form was frozen by D32 section 4 and may return only by re-registration under D37; the integer SpiralCore/FBS transport is exactly the substrate D32 names as the backbone, and is the ACTIVE model path.

never_tested: Training the float projection: zero optimizer updates have run on it, and no language measure exists.
Whether the root-edge secant surrogate yields descent; the pair credit is declared, not proved.
Whether one selected atom per output block carries enough information compared with an all-input mixing projection (no capacity or cost comparison was run).
Input-conditioned behaviour: selection by shared learned queries does not by itself make the read depend on the input.
Coverage of all 240 E8 roots (only one 16-root anchor orbit) and an independent H4 partner; the complete marked external FBS object.
Tokens/s or energy against the retired dense arm, and any D11 export of the float form.
failed_only_on_configuration: Starling tree recall 0.329 vs bar 0.54: the tree kept the source (hit rate 0.99 on seed 1) while the rank-table readout failed to turn it into an answer (recall 0.03); a readout failure, not a transport failure.
First discrete A2 pilot: loss rose while ranks improved, traced to an initializer with 16 distinct vectors and a writer that reached fewer target cells.
F32 secant control 11 failure: two F32 sums differing by about 8e-5 against a rounding floor near 1e-6, an instrument defect.
Setup blockers preserved as non-results: missing /usr/bin/time, fixture credit inferred as F64 instead of F32, an orphaned test comment, the first discrete attempt's CUDA launch-resource stop.
The dense Hamilton contraction it replaced was retired by rule (D25), not by a measured negative.
open_questions: Does selecting one atom per output block lose too much compared with the all-pair sum, and can a small routed set per block recover it?
Is the secant surrogate a sound credit signal, and can it be compared with the discrete counterfactual-and-choose rule on the same carrier?
How many 8D blocks are enough? The bound of 6,560 atoms is operational, not a quality bar, and no MiniLM 384D dependency is adopted.
Would a float SpiralCore trunk under D37 add anything beyond the integer discrete path that already runs, or only duplicate it at higher cost?

figure_ideas: A base-3 tree of atoms, with one root-to-leaf path highlighted; beside it the 16 roots of the E8 anchor orbit as nodes of the 15-edge BFS graph. Move the query point: the nearest root changes, and the chosen atom's 8 coordinates travel along the BFS edges, each edge permuting axes and flipping signs; then run the same path backward to show the exact inverse.

A route diagram of two SpiralCore edges applied to a concrete 8-vector (for example the root (1,1,0,0,0,0,0,0)), showing coordinate permutation and sign flips step by step, then composing two steps into one signed action and checking it equals the product.

Dense vs selected projection side by side: a grid where every input block connects to every output block (all cells lit) against a grid with exactly one line per output block, labelled with the one atom each output block chose.
